methods.label: Compare both terms with one half
methods.explanation:
The square root requires \(x\ge0\). The two terms must add to \(1\), so try making each term \(1/2\). Setting \(4x=1/2\) gives \(x=1/8\), and this also makes
\[
\sqrt{2x}=\sqrt{\frac14}=\frac12.
\]
Thus \(x=1/8\) satisfies the equation.

To prove that it is the only solution, consider the other allowed values. If \(0\le x<1/8\), then \(4x<1/2\) and \(\sqrt{2x}<1/2\), so their sum is less than \(1\). If \(x>1/8\), both terms are greater than \(1/2\), so their sum is greater than \(1\). These cases exclude every other real value.

Therefore \(x=\boxed{1/8}\), a rational number that is not an integer. It is fractional, choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
methods.levelReason: The proof needs only rational arithmetic, principal square roots, and order comparisons. The comparison argument establishes uniqueness without a quadratic equation.
